title: Leader, manager and how a band ends a number with one stop
summary: Barnes says it does not matter whether the clarinetist or trombonist leads; the leader kicks off and signals one stop before the last chorus.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Big band discipline versus small-group freedom

blocks.x: Do you think it's all right to have the trombone for the leader of the band? Or is it best for the have the carnet to be the leader and call the tunes and stomp off and all? Or the clarinetist?
Does it make any real difference?

It doesn't make no difference. It makes no difference who he's managing. But even now, at that, the manager don't call to him. You understand what I mean? Really? He's a businessman. See, now I could say, let's go over and play a tiger ring. Well, I was going to play. He says, all right, then next we'll play that. Well, let's play that and sing right after that. Well, each man pick a number that makes it go make the job finish up. You understand?
Well, who usually stumps off the band, mainly? Who knocks off the band?
Well, the leader. The leader knocks off. The leader knocks the band off. He puts it off and knocks it off. See, that's all.
Well, now when you want to go out, supposing you're coming to the last chorus and you're going to go out on the last chorus, how do you let the band know that you're going to go out? Knock it off.
Knock it off. One stop, huh?
When do you hit that one stop?
Just before you get to the last chorus?
Do you do it during the last chorus or do you do it right before you go into the last chorus? Right before you go into the last chorus.

That's the best time to stop. Right before you go into the last chorus, you make it, well, then know that chorus is putting you on end. You know what I'm saying? Now after you're going to pick up and start off, you're going to maintain. That's the return, get you in and get ready. Look, come on, you're ready. See? Some will hit you this, some will hit you that. But your right wing is dash. That's the old way.
That's the old time wing. See, when you hit dash, pick up and get ready when you're ready. Let's go.
